first_impression.reaction: My assistant found it searching Seminyak. The first screen is calm. No prices, no 'dream day', and the takeaways admit that none of these places publishes exclusive use, which is the thing I need to know. But Seminyak is a busy strip, and most of these spaces are sized for 50 to 100 people. Her summary would be: 'Only W and Alila take 200 or more, nothing can be closed, there's a good list of privacy questions, nothing on security or private arrivals.' I read the takeaways, the table, the guest-count grid, W and Alila, the privacy questions and the close.

journey.quote: None of the seven publishes exclusive use of the whole property, so ask in writing whether your ceremony and reception spaces can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it's the right question on the first screen. It also tells me straight away that Seminyak probably isn't where we can close a whole property.

journey.quote: Use this grid to narrow by numbers. Each figure is the venue's own, for the space named.
journey.reaction: Useful. My assistant goes straight to '150 and more' and stops there. That's two venues.

journey.quote: The Ice Garden, described as a beachfront reception venue, takes 100 for a reception or 70 for a banquet, and the WET Deck takes 300 for a reception or 200 for a banquet.
journey.reaction: At last, a space that can physically take us, with separate rooms for each night of the weekend. But W is a lively hotel full of other guests.

journey.quote: Packages include rates on group bookings.
journey.reaction: Packages and group rates. That's discount talk. It isn't how I want my wedding described.
Fifty guests. Not for us. Skipped.

journey.quote: The Truly Lovely Oasis package includes flower girls and umbrella boys in Balinese costume, with a choir or Balinese rindik bamboo music.
journey.reaction: A named package as the standout. It reads like a brochure for standard clients, and the costumed children feel like a set piece, not real cultural care.

journey.quote: It opens to the public from 10am to 9pm daily, so ask early about private hire and how late music can run.
journey.reaction: A public pool club with a dive tower. That's the opposite of discretion. I can't see why it's on a list I'd read.

journey.section: On the sand or around a pool
journey.quote: On a public beach, decide early how much of the view you want to share.
journey.reaction: Good, the page knows the beach is public. That's exactly my worry about Seminyak.

journey.section: Security and privacy: questions for any couple
journey.quote: What are the rules on drones, outside photographers and guests posting on social media?
journey.reaction: This is the first section written with someone like me in mind. Screening from the beach, guest-only areas, drones, social media. I'd add one more: how our own security team works with the venue's.

journey.section: How do guests get to Seminyak?
journey.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
journey.reaction: Written for a group chat of friends. People whose job it is handle our guests' travel.

journey.section: How do guests get to Seminyak?
journey.quote: Does the venue arrange guest transport, and for how many guests?
journey.reaction: Nothing about private transfers, VIP arrivals or moving known guests through the airport quietly. My family office would ask that first.

journey.section: Shortlist your Seminyak venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One contact suits me, because fewer people means fewer leaks. But 'for Australian couples' tells me I'm not who this was written for, and nothing shows a wedding at our size.

unanswered_questions: Have you delivered a wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
Who would be on the ground in Bali for us, and do you have direct relationships with W Bali Seminyak or Alila Seminyak? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private airport arrivals, transfers and coordination between our security team and the venue's? (deferred business detail)
Can you quote in a currency other than AUD, and do you work through a family office? (deferred business detail)
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, staff phones, press? (deferred business detail)
Can W Bali Seminyak or Alila Seminyak close the property, or a whole wing, to the public for three days?
Can the WET Deck and Great Room be screened from the public beach and other hotel guests?
If Seminyak can't be closed, which part of Bali can take 300 guests in private?

turn_offs_found.quote: Packages include rates on group bookings.
turn_offs_found.why: Package and discount language. It frames the wedding as a group deal, not a private event.

turn_offs_found.quote: The Truly Lovely Oasis package includes flower girls and umbrella boys in Balinese costume, with a choir or Balinese rindik bamboo music.
turn_offs_found.why: Leads with a named package as the standout, so it reads like a set menu for standard clients.

turn_offs_found.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explains traveller basics to a family whose guests' travel is handled for them.

turn_offs_found.quote: There have been cases of methanol poisoning in Bali, and as little as one shot can be fatal, so serve and order only branded alcohol.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. It's a backpacker warning, not advice for a private event with its own caterer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
turn_offs_found.why: Frames the service around a standard Australian couple. I live in Dubai, so it tells me I'm outside the audience.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the W Bali Seminyak capacities, the Alila 250 figure and the privacy question list in the planning file, and send the volcano and flight-disruption lines to whoever handles guest travel. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Seminyak venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=seminyak-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a blog link. The page is honest and the privacy questions are good, but nothing here can be closed for us, it says nothing about security, private arrivals or work at our scale, and it's addressed to Australian couples. I'd want a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Add one question to the security and privacy list about the couple's own security team working with the venue's, and add a private airport arrivals and transfers question to the transport list. Phrase both as questions to ask venues, not as brand claims.
Lead W Bali Seminyak and The Seminyak Beach Resort with their spaces rather than 'packages', 'group booking rates' and the named package as the standout.
Cut the passport-damage and methanol lines down to one pointer to Smartraveller for readers who delegate guest travel.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

open_questions.question: Seminyak is structurally a weak fit for Layla: there is no published exclusive use and only two venues take 200 or more. Low relevance is a destination limit, not a draft flaw. Weigh it against the 0.20 persona weight.

assumptions: Layla's assistant found the post through a search for 'seminyak wedding venues' while shortlisting. Layla read the summary, takeaways, tables, W and Alila, the privacy questions, travel and the close.
The persona is provisional and not calibrated with the CRM, so confidence is 0.75.
